classification.difficultyReason: Dissect the quadrilateral at the diagonal intersection and combine four triangle areas using supplementary-angle sine equality.

content.prompt: A quadrilateral has diagonals of length $12\text{ cm}$ and $18\text{ cm}$. If the angle between the diagonals is $65^\circ$, find the area of the quadrilateral, correct to the nearest square centimetre.

answer.short:
$98\text{ cm}^2$.

Split the quadrilateral into four triangles at the diagonal intersection and apply the triangle area rule.
answer.worked:
Let the diagonals intersect at $O$. Let the two segments of one diagonal have lengths $x$ and $y$, and those of the other have lengths $u$ and $v$, in centimetres. Thus $x+y=12$ and $u+v=18$.

The four angles at $O$ alternate between $65^\circ$ and $115^\circ$. Since $\sin115^\circ=\sin65^\circ$, adding the four triangle areas gives:
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12xu\sin65^\circ+\frac12yu\sin65^\circ+\frac12yv\sin65^\circ+\frac12xv\sin65^\circ\\A&=\frac12(x+y)(u+v)\sin65^\circ\\A&=\frac12(12)(18)\sin65^\circ\\A&=108\sin65^\circ\text{ cm}^2\\A&\approx98\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
